title: Chapter 174: The Monster's Weakness
html:
“The youngest persona? Men Nan’s third personality is deeply withdrawn and rarely appears. I can’t promise I’ll be able to do anything, so you should prepare yourself for failure.” On Doctor Gao’s end of the call, a door opened. He was already hurrying out of his home.

“Only the youngest persona can answer my question. Doctor Gao, no matter what it takes, you have to wake him up!” The door behind Chen Ge slammed again, the sound carrying clearly through the phone.

“I’ll do my best!” Doctor Gao had met Chen Ge through Gao Ru Xue. At first, he had regarded him merely as someone interested in psychology. But after Chen Ge volunteered to help Wang Xin and Men Nan, his opinion of the young man improved considerably—though he also found himself with many new questions about him.

In particular, Doctor Gao had witnessed something suspicious at Hai Ming Apartments that night, but he had told no one. He kept it to himself, determined to find the answer on his own. The call remained connected as Doctor Gao drove toward Men Nan’s hospital and Chen Ge struggled to hold the door behind him shut.

Three minutes passed, but the pounding on the door showed no sign of stopping. Worse still, the sound of a lock disengaging came from nearby Room 8. Its reinforced door slowly opened a crack.

An asymmetrical face peered out. The man craned his neck through the gap, then emerged in a doctor’s coat.

“So he was hiding in the ward.” Chen Ge had tried to open that door earlier and failed. In retrospect, the twisted-faced man had probably tampered with it. The Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer was propped against the door to Room 3, leaving Chen Ge with only the cleaver.

He studied the twisted-faced man, considering whether to shove him through the blood-red door as well.

“I wonder what happens to a living person trapped behind that door. If he attacks me, he’ll make the perfect test subject.” The greater the danger, the calmer Chen Ge became. Keeping hold of the cleaver, he adjusted the hammer into a makeshift barricade. Even if he moved away, the door would not open immediately.

Since midnight, subtle changes had come over the man’s distorted face. His expression had grown more deranged, and he now advanced on Chen Ge slowly, his hands empty.

“Something’s wrong.” Chen Ge spotted the discrepancy at once. In the second sick hall, the man had fled without hesitation despite carrying an axe. Yet here in the third sick hall, he dared approach Chen Ge empty-handed when Chen Ge had both a cleaver and a hammer.

The white cat let out a threatening hiss. It had leaped from Chen Ge’s shoulder during his fight with the nurse and now bared its teeth at the twisted-faced man. Confronted by the man and the cat, the twisted face wore an expression utterly unlike before. His surgically altered features pulled into an ugly smile.

His pace slowed with every step, as though a tremendous weight pressed down on his shoulders and each movement caused him agony.

“His pose is similar to Wang Shenglong’s…”

Chen Ge held the cleaver before his chest as the sight he least wanted to see unfolded. The man’s lips split wider, and a second head rose from behind his shoulders.

The head itself looked ordinary, but beneath it, a thin monster nearly two and a half meters long unfurled from the man’s back like someone rising to their feet. Its lower body remained fused to him, while its upper body easily brushed the ceiling before curving forward like a cobra with a human head.

“What is that?” Chen Ge had prepared himself, yet the creature still shocked him. It was unnaturally long and thin, draped in a large piece of crudely stitched white cloth. Through gaps in the fabric, he could make out several silent, drawn human faces.

The monster probably had not always been so tall. Only after climbing onto people’s shoulders and consuming them had it grown to this size. A realization struck Chen Ge. Wang Shenglong had once depicted his relationship with the monster in a drawing: Wang Shenglong stood beneath it, supporting the creature on his shoulders.

But the twisted-faced man shared a different relationship with the creature before Chen Ge. This monster emerged directly from his back.

Is the twisted-faced man the monster itself, or have the two formed some kind of symbiotic relationship?

He had no time to dwell on it. Although the man stopped two meters away, the elongated creature on his back had already stretched over Chen Ge’s head. Its face was so ordinary that one could forget it at a glance. Who would have imagined such a mundane face concealing something so grotesque?

“Let’s play a game. If you win, I’ll let you go. If you lose, you’ll give me your body.” The monster’s lips moved in perfect unison with the twisted-faced man’s, and its voice sounded directly inside Chen Ge’s mind. “The game is called ‘Who Speaks First.’”

It was a game the victim was destined to lose because it had no time limit. Wang Shenglong was the perfect example. Once someone accepted, the monster would climb onto their back and begin its torment.

If the victim lost their resolve and spoke, the monster won. Even if they remained silent, however, it would stay perched on their shoulders and the game would never end. The faces visible through the gaps in its shroud likely belonged to its former victims.

“If you want to play a game, fine. But we’ll have to change the rules,” Chen Ge replied calmly. Doctor Gao was still rushing to the hospital, so Chen Ge needed to buy time.

The monster halted half a meter above his head and drew a shallow breath, apparently baffled by his response. After a brief pause, it glanced at the twisted-faced man as if seeking his opinion. Shouldn’t a normal person be screaming by now?

The man’s smile froze. Apparently deciding that Chen Ge was mocking them, he pointed at Chen Ge’s head. The monster understood. It bent lower, its body continuing to uncoil as a pair of shriveled hands reached for Chen Ge’s face.

Chen Ge watched it approach without losing his composure. If anything, his thoughts became sharper than ever.

That’s its weakness! When it attacked, only its upper body moved; its lower half remained attached to the twisted-faced man. It probably can’t move that part freely.

No wonder it tricks people into playing. If it could simply leap onto someone’s shoulders and seize their body, it wouldn’t need the game as an excuse.

Chen Ge stepped back, his eyes gleaming. The moment it transfers from one body to another must be when it’s most vulnerable.
